title: Why Is It So Hard to Lose Weight Once You're Working?
intro: It's not because you're lazy or lack discipline. Work routines like sitting for long hours, eating around meeting schedules and not getting enough sleep really do make weight harder to lose, but all of this can be managed bit by bit.

sections.p: From home into the car, sitting in traffic, sitting in front of the laptop, then going home and sitting again. Many working women only reach an estimated 3,000 to 4,000 steps a day. These small daily movements actually burn a lot of energy, so when they're gone, weight goes up easily even if your eating hasn't changed much.

sections.h: Eating according to your work schedule, not your hunger
sections.p: Skipping breakfast in the morning because you're rushing. Late lunch because of meetings. Kuih and sweet drinks in the pantry in the afternoon. Then at night you're very hungry, so you eat a big meal. This pattern makes it harder to control portions.
When you sleep less than 6 hours, many people feel hungrier and crave more sweet food. Work stress also makes us look for food to feel better. This is common, not a personal weakness.

Nasi campur, mamak and kedai kopi can all fit into a weight-loss plan. The challenge is the extra kuah, oil, fried dishes and sweet drinks that we don't count. So the issue is portion and frequency, not the food itself.

Conditions like PCOS, thyroid problems or certain medications can affect weight and appetite. If your periods are irregular, you're always very tired, or your weight goes up for no clear reason, get checked by a doctor. If you might be pregnant, talk to your doctor first before changing how you eat.

action: Add an estimated 2,000 steps a day, for example a 10-minute walk after lunch and taking the stairs for one floor.
Don't let lunch get too late. Keep a boiled egg or fruit in your bag for days with long meetings.
Sleep 30 minutes earlier on at least 3 nights this week.
Swap one sweet drink a day for a less-sweet version or plain water.
myth: Many believe eating once a day is the fastest way to lose weight. Actually, skipping meals often makes you too hungry and overeat at night. What matters is how much you eat across the whole day, not how many times you eat.

faq.q: How fast should my weight go down?
faq.a: A realistic target is an estimated 0.5 to 1 kg a week. Some weeks your weight won't move, and that's normal. Look at the trend over 3 to 4 weeks, not your weight on one day.

faq.q: Do I need to join a gym?
faq.a: Not compulsory. Strength exercises at home 2 to 3 times a week, for example squats, wall push-ups and lunges, plus more walking, already help.
Yes. Try filling an estimated quarter of your plate with rice, a quarter with protein and half with vegetables. No need to cut out rice, just manage the portion.
